title: Impact of FTX's Bankruptcy on Singapore's Financial Markets, Regulation of Asset Classes and Strategies of Investment Entities
what_it_is: Impact of FTX's Bankruptcy on Singapore's Financial Markets, Regulation of Asset Classes and Strategies of Investment Entities

sections.label: MAS regulation of digital token providers
sections.summary: Questions ask whether MAS will regulate digital token providers and exchanges for liquidity, and about FTX losses and domino effects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister whether MAS intends to regulate digital token service providers and exchanges to ensure liquidity requirements so as to safeguard customers' digital tokens from insolvency risks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister (a) what is the magnitude of losses incurred by Singaporean retail investors and individuals affected by cryptocurrency trading platform FTX’s collapse; and (b) whether FTX’s collapse will have a domino effect on other cryptocurrency exchanges.

sections.label: Temasek FTX investment and exposure
sections.summary: Questions ask the value of Temasek's FTX investments, Singapore investors' exposure, and effects on Singaporeans and MAS consultation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister (a) what is the value of Temasek Holdings’ investments in cryptocurrency trading platform FTX and its subsidiaries when FTX filed for bankruptcy in the United States on 11 November 2022; (b) whether the Government has any data on the exposure of Singapore investors to FTX in terms of the number of investors and the total value of their holdings; (c) whether FTX’s sudden bankruptcy will affect (i) Singaporeans and (ii) MAS' ongoing consultation in relation to consumer harm from cryptocurrency trading; and (d) if so, how.

sections.label: Temasek FTX loss and NIRC
sections.summary: Questions ask the financial loss suffered by Temasek from FTX's collapse and whether it affects Net Investment Returns Contribution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance in light of the collapse of cryptocurrency trading platform FTX (a) what is the financial loss suffered by Temasek Holdings; and (b) whether this will affect the Net Investment Returns Contribution for the next three financial years.

sections.label: Audit of Temasek and GIC
sections.summary: Question asks whether the Government will add Temasek and GIC to Auditor-General audit and Public Accounts Committee oversight.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance as Temasek Holdings and GIC are Fifth Schedule entities, whether the Government will consider adding the two sovereign wealth funds to the audit ambit of the Auditor-General's Office and oversight by the Public Accounts Committee, on the condition that commercially sensitive elements in any audit report be made available to legislators but redacted from published reports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We have drawn a sharp distinction between growing an innovative and responsible digital asset ecosystem, and speculation in cryptocurrency, which we actively discourage for the retail public.

sections.label: Limited FTX spillovers assessment
sections.summary: The assessment is that spillovers from the FTX collapse to Singapore's financial system and economy will be very limited.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: As for Singapore’s broader financial system and economy, our assessment is that spillovers from the FTX collapse will be very limited.

sections.label: MAS investor protection measures for DPT
sections.summary: MAS plans basic investor protection measures for licensed DPT service providers, including risk awareness tests, asset segregation and trading platform restrictions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Going forward, MAS plans to introduce some basic investor protection measures for DPT service providers which are licensed in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: MAS recently published a consultation paper, which includes proposals that DPT service providers, amongst other things: (a) administer a risk awareness test to evaluate if potential retail customers are suitable for accessing cryptocurrency services; (b) segregate customers’ assets from their own assets so as to prevent lending out of customers’ money and protect customer interests should the service provider fail; and (c) refrain from operating a trading platform while simultaneously taking proprietary positions for their own account, to prevent conflicts of interest.

sections.label: Temasek GIC digital assets exposure
sections.summary: Temasek and GIC have some digital assets investments but no direct cryptocurrency exposure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Insofar as blockchain technology is concerned, Temasek and GIC have some investments in the digital assets space, but they have no direct exposure to cryptocurrencies.

sections.label: FTX write-off and NIRC
sections.summary: Temasek's early-stage portfolio returned mid-teens over the last decade, and the FTX loss will not impact the NIRC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: After writing off the FTX investment, Temasek's early-stage portfolio, as of March this year, has generated an internal rate of return in the mid-teens over the last decade, better than industry averages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The FTX loss will also not impact the Net Investment Returns Contribution (NIRC), as the NIRC is tied to the overall expected long-term returns of our investment entities and not to individual investments.

sections.label: MOF responds to entity questions
sections.summary: MOF will respond to Parliamentary questions on entity performance, so no additional audit requirements or Parliamentary Committees are needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In Parliament, if there are any questions by Members about the performance of the entities, MOF will respond to them, as we are doing now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: There is, therefore, no need for additional audit requirements or Parliamentary Committees.

sections.label: Early-stage and digital asset exposure
sections.summary: Temasek's early-stage exposure is about 6% of its portfolio, and both entities' digital asset investments are within limited parameters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Within that, it has limited exposure to early-stage companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And within that space, it has exposure to early-stage companies, but Temasek itself has put out a statement to explain that its exposure to early-stage companies is about, presently, 6% of its overall portfolio.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For both entities, this exposure to early-stage companies would include investments in digital assets, but it would be diversified to a broad range of different sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, to answer the question: yes, there will be other companies in the digital asset space that GIC and Temasek have invested in, but they are within these limited parameters.

sections.label: MAS assesses financial sector exposure
sections.summary: MAS has assessed that Singapore financial institutions' exposure to cryptocurrencies and digital assets is very limited.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: As I mentioned just now in my reply, MAS has assessed and determined that for the financial sector itself, financial institutions based here in Singapore, our exposure to cryptocurrencies and the digital assets is very limited.

sections.label: Government shareholder governance role
sections.summary: The Government does not micro-manage investments but appoints board members and senior management and holds them accountable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In our case, we have put in place a very strong governance process and system, where the Government is a shareholder – we do not micro-manage, we do not decide on investments, we do not prescribe asset classes or assets – but we have a role in appointing board members, senior management and we hold them accountable to delivering good, long-term performance.

sections.label: Monitoring versus prescribing boards
sections.summary: Monitoring assets and geographies is done because monitoring is not prescribing, leaving boards to decide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: On Mr Leon Perera's question on how do you square the monitoring of assets, geographies and all that, with the policy of leaving the boards to make their own decisions, well, we do it because monitoring is not prescribing.

sections.label: MAS customer asset segregation
sections.summary: MAS is looking into segregating customers' assets from company assets and preventing DPT providers from operating a trading platform taking proprietary positions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: MAS is looking into segregating customers' assets from the company's own assets so that there is a very strict prohibition from lending out of customers' money, which was what happened in the case of FTX.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: MAS is also looking at one of the proposals to ensure that the DPT service provider does not operate a separate trading platform that simultaneously takes proprietary positions.

sections.label: Cryptocurrency has no intrinsic value
sections.summary: Even a well-run, well-managed platform's cryptocurrency itself has no intrinsic value.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Even if a platform is well-run, well-managed, the cryptocurrency itself has no intrinsic value.

sections.label: Temasek update to MOF
sections.summary: Temasek has provided an update to MOF on its findings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: On the second question, on their reports, yes, Temasek has provided an update to MOF on its findings.

sections.label: Temasek statement on FTX investment
sections.summary: GIC and Temasek do not disclose specific investments, but Temasek issued a statement on its investment decision after reputational damage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, as a matter of practice, GIC and Temasek, in fact, do not put out any information on specific individual investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But in this case, precisely because of the unique circumstances leading up to it – because from Temasek's point of view, it recognised that it has incurred reputational damage – Temasek decided to put out a statement disclosing the circumstances leading up to its investment decision, why it had done all the due diligence and, despite the due diligence, found reasons to still proceed with the investment.

sections.label: MAS consultation papers before FTX
sections.summary: MAS published consultation papers with tighter regulatory measures even before the FTX collapse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: As I have highlighted, MAS has published, even before the FTX collapse, a series of consultation papers with tighter regulatory measures.

sections.label: Auditor-General audits of Temasek
sections.summary: Temasek is not subject to Auditor-General audits, but the Auditor-General can be asked to conduct a full audit if reasons arise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: So, why is it then that Temasek is not subject to the Auditor-General's audits?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But, in fact, where there are issues that come up – could be in a Town Council, it could be in a Statutory Board, it could be in Temasek – if there are reasons, we will have no hesitation to ask the Auditor-General to go in to do a full audit.

sections.label: GIC and Temasek performance
sections.summary: GIC and Temasek have done well compared with other leading institutional investors amid a more challenging investment environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The facts remain that even after comparing GIC and Temasek with other leading institutional investors, our two investment entities have done well, creditably, amidst a more challenging investment environment.

sections.label: Temasek and GIC portfolio performance
sections.summary: The overall portfolios of Temasek and GIC have performed creditably, in many instances above industry averages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: As I mentioned just now, if you look at the overall portfolio for both Temasek and GIC, their performance has been creditable and, in fact, in many instances, above industry averages.

sections.label: Temasek's FTX investment
sections.summary: Temasek's investment in FTX was US$275 million, a small percentage of its overall portfolio.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Second, I note that Temasek's investment in FTX, at US$275 million, was a small percentage of their overall portfolio.

sections.label: Limited exposures in diversified portfolio
sections.summary: Exposures are limited within a well-diversified portfolio, allowing good returns on other projects despite some losses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We do not go beyond that because we do not go into specific company investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But within that broad context and the parameters I have set out, I hope Members are assured that the exposures are limited and it is within the context of a very well-diversified portfolio, which will then allow us to still earn good returns on other projects, even though there may well be a few projects where there are losses.

sections.label: Thresholds for AGO audit
sections.summary: Any audit of a Temasek investment or process will be led by people separate from the investment team that made the decision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The second question is, what thresholds must be crossed before AGO steps in to audit a Temasek investment or Temasek investment process in a company?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: It will be led by people who are separate from the investment team that made this decision.

sections.label: Auditor-General audit threshold conditions
sections.summary: Government may not rule out commissioning an audit if there is significant investment loss, negligence, fraud or misconduct.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I think it is the question that the Leader of the Opposition raised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Certainly, the Government will not rule out doing so, but it is not just a matter of an investment loss.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: It would be something that we feel has gone wrong within the organisation, possibly there might be negligence, there might be fraud, there might be misconduct.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, it has to be of that significant threshold for us to say, "Look, something is not right within the organisation; let us commission or get the Auditor-General to go in and do a proper audit and investigation".

sections.label: Long-term investment horizon for entities
sections.summary: Entities should invest long-term within risk limits, including in new technologies and early-stage companies, accepting many startups fail.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: That is not something we want to do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We want our entities to have that long-term horizon, invest within the risk limits, invest in some new technologies, some early-stage companies, recognising that, as I said just now, many startups will not do well, but a few might eventually prove to be wildly successful and become giants in their own right.
